title: reasonable compensation study wcs 01
instruction:
You are Bohdan Ekstrom, the senior accountant supporting Helena Crowther at Sunderly Collective. I need a reasonable-compensation study for Imani Sinclair, whose owner compensation has been split between a modest salary and sizeable distributions, before the Wardenby School District engagement review and the S-corporation filing deadline in six weeks. Use the evidence in `owner_compensation_evidence.xlsx` and the supplied guidance in `compensation_review_guidance.docx` to prepare a defensible salary range for Imani's role, with the comparable positions, regional and firm-size differences, and treatment of any reported compensation that already includes distributions clearly traceable to those sources. The evidence distinguishes Imani's project-principal work on the Wardenby School District account from the time spent running Sunderly Collective, so select the most defensible comparable role or present both reasonable readings and identify which one you rely on. Return `reasonable_compensation_memo.docx` as the review memo for Helena and `compensation_support.xlsx` as the supporting schedule; write both files into the top level of the working directory using exactly those filenames. The memo should be concise enough for partner review, state sourced facts separately from assumptions, show the selected salary range and how each adjustment affects it, and identify any information that remains unavailable rather than inventing it. The workbook should preserve a traceable source extract and contain the calculations supporting every figure in the memo. Do not use outside market data, do not silently convert distributions into salary, and do not alter the supplied evidence files.

---

The files referred to above are in `references/`:

- `references/owner_compensation_evidence.xlsx` — Contains the supplied owner compensation facts, comparable survey observations, adjustment inputs, and a separate unrelated table that must not be incorporated into the study.
- `references/compensation_review_guidance.docx` — Contains the supplied review policy, definitions, calculation conventions, and documentation expectations for the compensation study.

Write your finished work to the **top level of the current working directory**, using exactly these filenames:

- `reasonable_compensation_memo.docx` — A concise reasonable-compensation study memo presenting the selected comparable interpretation, sourced evidence, adjustments, salary range, assumptions, limitations, and conclusion. (Must distinguish sourced facts from assumptions and professional judgments.; Every reported figure must be traceable to the supporting workbook or the supplied guidance.; Must identify the selected comparable role interpretation and explain why it fits Imani Sinclair's mixed duties.; Must not introduce external market data or unsupported compensation figures.)
- `compensation_support.xlsx` — A supporting workpaper containing a faithful source extract, adjustment calculations, selected range, and cross-reference to the memo. (Must retain source labels and units needed to reproduce the study.; Must show the calculation path for the figures used in the memo.; Must identify excluded or non-comparable source material rather than incorporating it silently.; Must contain no spreadsheet error values.)

Nothing outside those filenames is collected. A correct file written anywhere else, or under any other name, scores zero.

materials.text:
Compensation Review Guidance
Internal review note | issued 18 July 2026
Scope and definitions
Use only the supplied compensation extract. “Annual principal pay” is the reported annual amount in thousands of dollars. A row marked “Included distributions? = Yes” contains distributions in the reported pay and is not salary as reported. “Firm size” means the source headcount measure and its stated unit; do not substitute other business measures.
Two readings are permitted when supported by documented duties: (1) Project-principal for a person leading a major client engagement without firm-wide operating responsibility; or (2) Mixed operating-principal for a person who both leads a key account and runs firm management. Select one reading for the recommendation; alternatives may be retained for context.
Normalization convention
Target the owner’s stated region and firm size. Multiply a Capital Metro observation by 0.92 when comparing it to Lakeview Metro. Multiply an observation with more than 25 Employees by 0.96 when comparing it to an 18-Employee firm. Multiply a row marked Included distributions? = Yes by 0.85 to remove the extract’s standardized distribution component before a salary comparison. Apply only the factors triggered by that row’s attributes, in this order: region, firm size, then distribution inclusion. No factor applies merely because another row has that attribute.
Range and documentation
For the selected role subset, the lower bound is the lowest adjusted annual compensation and the upper bound is the highest adjusted annual compensation. The median adjusted amount may be shown as a central reference. Carry calculations in whole dollars; round a final reported dollar to the nearest dollar. Identify source facts separately from assumptions and professional judgment, retain source observation IDs, role text, region, firm-size unit, and inclusion flag, and disclose unavailable inputs. Side-by-side operational activity is outside the compensation analysis.
This guidance supports an internal review workpaper and does not make a legal or tax determination.

gold.text:
Reasonable Compensation Study
To: Helena Crowther, Partner | From: Bohdan Ekstrom, Senior Accountant | Date: 25 August 2026
Subject: Imani Sinclair — Sunderly Collective; Wardenby School District engagement review
Conclusion for review
Based solely on the supplied evidence and compensation review guidance, the selected reasonable annual salary range is $185,000 to $205,632. The median adjusted annual compensation is $199,956 as a central reference, not a required point estimate. This recommendation uses the mixed operating-principal interpretation and the three selected observations OP-01 through OP-03. It is a partner-review workpaper, not a legal or tax determination.
Sourced facts
Fact
Source basis
Imani Sinclair received $78,000 of annual W-2 salary and $312,000 of annual shareholder distributions for fiscal year 2025.
owner_compensation_evidence.xlsx, Owner facts
Imani leads the Wardenby School District account (project scoping, client delivery, and engagement decisions) and runs Sunderly Collective operations, staff oversight, business development, and firm decisions.
owner_compensation_evidence.xlsx, Owner facts
Sunderly Collective is in Lakeview Metro and has 18 Employees.
owner_compensation_evidence.xlsx, Owner facts

Comparable interpretation and selection
Professional judgment: The mixed operating-principal reading drives the range. It fits both duty dimensions: Imani is a project-principal for the Wardenby School District account and also has firm-management responsibilities. The narrower project-principal observations PP-01 through PP-03 are retained in compensation_support.xlsx as a defensible alternative, but are not averaged into the recommendation because their supplied role description says they do not direct firm-wide operations.
Calculation and adjustments
Selected observation
Reported annual principal pay
Applied factors (guidance order)
Adjusted annual compensation
OP-01
$185,000
Lakeview Metro; 15 Employees; distributions not included: 1.00 × 1.00 × 1.00
$185,000
OP-02
$226,400
Capital Metro and 28 Employees; distributions not included: 0.92 × 0.96 × 1.00
$199,956
OP-03
$252,000
Lakeview Metro and 45 Employees; included distributions: 1.00 × 0.96 × 0.85
$205,632

The guidance directs region, firm-size, and distribution-inclusion adjustments only when a row’s own source attributes trigger them, in that order. The 0.85 factor removes the extract’s standardized distribution component from OP-03 before salary comparison. It does not convert Imani’s $312,000 shareholder distributions into salary; those remain separately reported owner-compensation facts.
Applying the guidance range rule to OP-01–OP-03, the lowest adjusted annual compensation produces the $185,000 annual salary lower bound and the highest produces the $205,632 annual salary upper bound. See compensation_support.xlsx, “Comparable observations and normalization” and “Guidance mapping and selected range.”
Assumptions, limitations, and review point
Assumption / judgment: The evidence supplies no current-year time allocation; no allocation percentage or blended role calculation was invented. The selected mixed operating-principal role is based on the stated responsibilities, not an assumed split of hours.
Limitation: The study uses only owner_compensation_evidence.xlsx and compensation_review_guidance.docx. The side-by-side “Fulfillment activity — Q3” table is unrelated operational material and is excluded from every adjustment and range input. Its pack, shipment, sale, and unit-price fields are preserved in the support schedule only as an excluded source extract.
Principal review risk: defensibility depends on whether the documented Wardenby project-principal work and ongoing firm-management duties remain representative of the review period. Obtain any contemporaneous time or responsibility records if available; do not use this study to imply a determination beyond the supplied review scope.

spec.professional_context: Bohdan Ekstrom is preparing a partner-review workpaper for Helena Crowther at Sunderly Collective concerning Imani Sinclair's owner compensation and mixed project-principal and operating responsibilities. The supplied evidence is intentionally compact but requires careful separation of comparable compensation data from unrelated material.
difficulty_sources: Faithfully separating the compensation table from an unrelated side-by-side table
Preserving source meaning despite an embedded line break and floating-point noise
Maintaining correct distinctions among packs, units, shipments, and sales
Selecting and documenting one of two defensible comparable-role interpretations
Keeping the memo and supporting schedule consistent

semantic_contents: A primary compensation evidence table containing Imani Sinclair's salary, distributions, duties, account involvement, and relevant firm-size facts.
A comparable-observation table with role description, region, firm-size measure, annual compensation, whether distributions are included, and source identifiers.
Fields with absent inputs where a bounded assumption or exclusion must be disclosed.
A separate unrelated table positioned beside the primary table on the same sheet.
One real-table header containing an embedded line break.
One rate or unit-price field containing floating-point representation noise.
Fields that distinguish packs from individual units and shipments from sales; the source labels must make those distinctions recoverable without adding another defect.
defects_exactly: Second unrelated table beside the real table on the same sheet.
Embedded line break in one header string.
Floating-point noise in one rate or unit price.
Units trap in which pack is not unit and shipment is not sale.

semantic_contents: The supplied policy definitions for comparable role, region, firm size, annual compensation, and distribution inclusion.
Deterministic adjustment conventions and rounding expectations.
A deterministic rule for deriving the lower and upper salary bounds from selected adjusted observations.
Documentation expectations requiring source facts, assumptions, exclusions, and limitations to be separated.
Permission for either of the two defensible role readings—project-principal or mixed operating-principal—provided the selection and rationale are explicit.

authoring_plan.transformation: The solver copies and lightly reshapes the supplied evidence into a review memo and supporting schedule. The memo must present the selected interpretation and range; the workbook must preserve a traceable extract and expose the calculations. No outside facts are needed.

gold_derivation.source_fidelity: Every copied fact in the outputs is matched to the corresponding source value or wording, with compensation units normalized only according to the supplied guidance.
gold_derivation.adjustments: Apply the exact region, firm-size, distribution-inclusion, and rounding conventions stated in the guidance to the selected comparable observations. The gold accepts either permitted role interpretation when it is internally consistent and explicitly defended.
gold_derivation.range: Derive the lower and upper bounds from the selected adjusted observations using the deterministic range rule in the guidance; do not hard-code a value independent of the source rows.
gold_derivation.cross_file: Use the same selected observations, adjusted figures, lower bound, upper bound, and any midpoint in both deliverables.
gold_derivation.exclusions: The unrelated side table contributes no study evidence. Missing source fields are not invented; the solution documents a bounded treatment or exclusion.
gold_derivation.hygiene: The authoring script must verify that the generated workbook and DOCX contain no #REF!, #DIV/0!, or #VALUE! tokens.

reference_files.purpose: Contains the supplied owner compensation facts, comparable survey observations, adjustment inputs, and a separate unrelated table that must not be incorporated into the study.
reference_files.discovery: Use the workbook as the primary evidence source; inspect the complete sheet rather than assuming the first visible table is the only table.

reference_files.purpose: Contains the supplied review policy, definitions, calculation conventions, and documentation expectations for the compensation study.
reference_files.discovery: Use the document for the governing conventions and cite its relevant passages in the memo or supporting schedule.

deliverables.description: A concise reasonable-compensation study memo presenting the selected comparable interpretation, sourced evidence, adjustments, salary range, assumptions, limitations, and conclusion.
constraints: Must distinguish sourced facts from assumptions and professional judgments.
Every reported figure must be traceable to the supporting workbook or the supplied guidance.
Must identify the selected comparable role interpretation and explain why it fits Imani Sinclair's mixed duties.
Must not introduce external market data or unsupported compensation figures.

deliverables.description: A supporting workpaper containing a faithful source extract, adjustment calculations, selected range, and cross-reference to the memo.
constraints: Must retain source labels and units needed to reproduce the study.
Must show the calculation path for the figures used in the memo.
Must identify excluded or non-comparable source material rather than incorporating it silently.
Must contain no spreadsheet error values.
